failureFirst.fail: THE SIGN AND THE SIZE OF THE RESIDUAL BOTH DEPEND ON THE HARNESS AND THE WINDOW. (1) Wave 251a's −0.143% is an order of magnitude above ⚡ (−0.020%) and 🪄 (−0.040%), while wave 270c's harness (20-periastron window, four-step extrapolation) reads −0.022% — SO 'THE LARGEST OF THE THREE' CANNOT BE STATED WITHOUT DECLARING THE WINDOW AND THE STEP. The closed form would ask for this system's own kappa*=12.003, and the frozen 12.0154 is used instead, so a 0.10% OVER-CANCELLATION IS BUILT IN — consistent with the measured −0.143%. (2) At the default dt=0.016 periastron detection itself breaks down (a pre-existing limit of a 1.88-hour orbit, unrelated to compactForce). (3) The residual changes sign between dt=0.008 and dt=0.004 (+2.46% → −1.19%), so the step trend is not a proof of convergence. (4) No action principle, no conservation law, energy does not close. (5) This is a development-set system, not a frozen hold-out.
failureFirst.pass: EVEN ON THE SYSTEM WITH THE LARGEST omega_dot OF ANY KNOWN DOUBLE NEUTRON STAR, ⚡'S SINGLE FROZEN kappa LANDS WITHIN 0.15%. Without moving any of 🩺's declarations, one added line moves the advance from +0.0110834°/orbit (about +100%) to +0.0055414°/orbit (−0.022% of the adopted record, on wave 270c's harness; wave 251a's harness read −0.143%). The gap between the frozen kappa and this system's own solution (12.0154 vs 12.0030, 0.10%) is identified as the leading term of the residual, so the residual is quantitatively accounted for as THE PRICE OF FREEZING rather than a bare disagreement. The unfitted periastron-to-periastron period (−0.0075%) is the best of the three.

THE SHORTEST-PERIOD NEUTRON-STAR BINARY IN THE GALAXY (1.88 hours), placed with ⚡'s recipe applied unchanged, as a hold-out (wave 248a — report 40). PSR J1946+2052 pairs a 16.96-ms pulsar with a neutron star at e=0.0638, and its periastron advance omega_dot=25.79205°/yr is the largest of any known double neutron star. THE ADOPTED RECORD IS ONE SET: Meng et al. 2025 A&A 704 A153, Table 1, DDFWHE column (Pb 0.07848805554(2) d = 6781.367998656 s, e 0.0638363(8), omega_dot 25.79205(40)°/yr — rows 285/289/290 of paper/data/solar-observations.csv; aligned into one set in wave 270c, with the previously adopted Stovall 2018 Pb/e kept as PREVIOUS). 1 unit = 10⁶ m / 10¹ s / 10²⁷ kg (the same L−T=5 family as ⚡📻🧮). Only gravity (E4), frame dragging (A8/E6′) and the geodesic 1PN term (E12) act — exactly as on ⚡. NOTHING IS CALIBRATED: f is ⚡'s linear-law fixed point evaluated once here, 1.9999655 (no fitted knob), and λ is the default (physics.spinSpin undeclared). The radius is the declared EOS proxy 11.75 km. The pulsar's observed 16.960-ms rotation is out of range and rides only the read-only spinDipole channel — AND THE COMPANION'S ROTATION IS UNOBSERVED, so no spinDipole is declared for it. physics.framePrecision:"double" removes the numerical floor.Measured (a 20-periastron window, periastron detection gated at 1.5 pi of cumulative orbital phase, double-precision dragging field — tests/exp-w270c-j1946adopt.mjs): PERIASTRON ADVANCE +0.0110920°/orbit (the dt sequence 0.016→0.008→0.004→0.002 gives 0.0116399→0.0112188→0.0110978→0.0110822, Richardson-extrapolated; apparent order 1.65 to 2.19). Against the adopted record's converted 0.0055424°/orbit the DFM/OBSERVED RATIO IS 2.00125. The unfitted side: the periastron-to-periastron period extrapolates to 6781.524 s (+0.0023% of 6781.367998656 s) and the eccentricity to 0.0638562 (+0.031% of 0.0638363). RUNNING THE SAME HARNESS ON THE PREVIOUS RECORD gives 6781.523 s, 0.0638679 and a ratio of 2.00128 — everything moved by less than 1e-5 relative. Sensitivity table (tests/exp-w248a.mjs): the companion spin over unobserved / assumed 10 ms / assumed 100 ms leaves 400 steps BIT-IDENTICAL, and radii of 11 / 11.75 / 13 km leave the periastron advance identical to 10 digits — only η moves, from 4.7e-14 to 9.1e-14 at an assumed 10 ms (three orders above ⚡'s 1.09e-16 at its OBSERVED spins, but that is a value produced by an ASSUMPTION). Zero NaN, zero clamps. Periods are judged only after their DEFINITION has been declared (adjudication I6, waves 249b→250d): the same-direction revolution and the periapsis-to-periapsis interval are different quantities; the verdict follows the periapsis definition, and where a system is near-circular that definition does not correspond to the observation, so it is annotated rather than judged.One-tap A/B: side B is kFrame=0 — at the same initial state and the same calibrated masses (×2.0) gravity is excessive and the orbit plunges (the machine control that these masses belong to kFrame=1 only). PUT ⚡ (J0737, omega_dot 16.90°/yr), 🧮 (J1757, 10.37°/yr) AND THIS SAMPLE (25.79°/yr) SIDE BY SIDE: across a 2.5x spread in omega_dot the DFM/observed ratio stays near 2 (⚡ 1.998 and 🧮 1.998 from their own waves' harnesses; this sample is 2.00125 on wave 270c's 20-periastron four-step extrapolation). Tapping the companion shows no spinDipole readout (the unobserved quantity is visibly absent). With timeScale=230 one orbit takes ~2.9 wall seconds; dispMag=1000 (display only).
